system_description.narrative_title: Fractured Global Order: War, Markets, Tech, and Strategic Competition
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is an open, stressed network shaped by simultaneous regional wars (notably the Iran conflict and the Russia–Ukraine war), intensified great-power strategic competition (China’s economic and Arctic push, Russia’s coordination with partners, US policy swings), and acute economic and financial turbulence (inflation, historic FX interventions, bond-market repricing). Rapid technological disruption—especially AI and cyber/biotech risks—interacts with supply‑chain shifts and climate-driven resource stress, producing cascading vulnerabilities across security, markets and governance. Domestic politics in major powers (US policy reversals and leadership choices) amplify systemic volatility and unpredictability.
system_description.scope: State actors and alliances; regional conflict theaters (Middle East, Black Sea/Ukraine, Korea); global markets and finance (FX, bonds, commodities); trade routes and critical supply chains (shipping chokepoints, Arctic corridors); major technology and corporate actors (AI, cyber, biotech); resource and climate stressors (droughts, energy flows).
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio‑technical‑economic system (global human civilization interacting with the biosphere, climate system, and planetary resource base).
adjacent_subsystems: Global Financial System & Markets (FX, bonds, commodities, central banks)
Great‑Power Strategic Competition (US–China–Russia dynamics and alliances)
Regional Conflict Theaters (Middle East, Ukraine/Black Sea, Korean Peninsula)
Global Technological & Cyber Ecosystem (AI, biotech, cyber security, major tech firms)

variables.name: Iran and Strait of Hormuz confrontation
variables.description: Iran, the United States, Gulf states and regional actors are contesting control of the Strait of Hormuz and adjacent sea lines as attacks, blockades and intensified economic pressure disrupt oil flows and raise risks of wider escalation.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine high‑intensity war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, supported respectively by Western aid and Russian mobilization, are locked in sustained high‑intensity conflict characterized by drone and missile strikes, Black Sea/port targeting and grinding frontline offensives that are reshaping military and economic balances in Europe.

variables.name: U.S.–China technology and supply‑chain rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are intensifying competition across semiconductors, AI, critical industrial supply chains and export controls as both sides and their firms push technological standards, market access and strategic autonomy.

variables.name: Global currency and macro‑policy pressure
variables.description: Major economies and policymakers (notably the United States, Japan and other central banks) are confronting one another through interventions, rapid policy shifts, market operations and tariff threats that are re‑ordering FX dynamics, yields and the political economy of financial influence.

variables.name: AI, biosecurity and cyber disruption
variables.description: Rapid advances in AI are producing a transnational power shift as state and corporate competition accelerates model development, fuels cyber insecurity and bio‑risk (including synthetic pathogens), and transforms labor markets while outpacing regulatory frameworks.
